extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies' EEO offices, agency counsel/HR, EEOC staff, and federal employees/complainants seeking to understand federal-sector EEO procedures and reporting requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and standards governing federal agencies' equal employment opportunity programs, complaint intake, pre‑complaint counseling, investigations, hearings, dismissals, remedies, and public data posting under 29 CFR Part 1614.

rubrics_metrics.name: General policy
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy of the Government of the United States to provide equal opportunity in employment for all persons and to prohibit discrimination in employment because of race; color; religion; sex; national origin; age; disability; genetic information; or pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions; and to promote equal employment opportunity through a continuing affirmative program in each agency. No person shall be subject to retaliation for opposing unlawful practices or participating in administrative or judicial proceedings under the covered statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency shall provide sufficient resources to EEO program
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall maintain a continuing affirmative program and 'provide sufficient resources to its equal employment opportunity program to ensure efficient and successful operation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt, fair and impartial processing of complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'provide for the prompt, fair and impartial processing of complaints in accordance with this part and the instructions contained in the Commission's Management Directives.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct continuing campaign to eradicate prejudice and discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'conduct a continuing campaign to eradicate every form of prejudice or discrimination from the agency's personnel policies, practices and working conditions.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate EEO policy and solicit recruitment broadly
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'communicate the agency's equal employment opportunity policy and program and its employment needs to all sources of job candidates without regard to protected characteristics; and solicit their recruitment assistance on a continuing basis.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and evaluate managerial/supervisory performance for EEO compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'review, evaluate and control managerial and supervisory performance... to insure a continuing affirmative application and vigorous enforcement of the policy of equal opportunity,' and provide orientation, training and advice to managers and supervisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary action for discriminatory practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'take appropriate disciplinary action against employees who engage in discriminatory practices.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodation for religious needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'make reasonable accommodation to the religious needs of applicants and employees when those accommodations can be made without undue hardship on the business of the agency.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodation for disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'make reasonable accommodation to the known physical or mental limitations of qualified applicants and employees with handicaps unless the accommodation would impose an undue hardship on the operation of the agency's program.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition for superior EEO accomplishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'provide recognition to employees, supervisors, managers and units demonstrating superior accomplishment in equal employment opportunity.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic evaluation of EEO program effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'establish a system for periodically evaluating the effectiveness of the agency's overall equal employment opportunity effort.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide employee development and training opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'provide the maximum feasible opportunity to employees to enhance their skills through on-the-job training, work-study programs and other training measures' so employees may advance according to ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform employees and labor organizations of EEO program and enlist cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'inform its employees and recognized labor organizations of the affirmative equal employment opportunity policy and program and enlist their cooperation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Community participation to improve employment opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'participate at the community level with other employers, schools and universities and other groups in cooperative action to improve employment opportunities and community conditions that affect employability.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must develop plans, procedures and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: To implement their EEO program agencies must 'develop the plans, procedures and regulations necessary to carry out its program.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish or make available ADR for pre‑complaint and formal processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'establish or make available an alternative dispute resolution program' and the program must be available for both pre‑complaint and formal complaint processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular appraisal of personnel operations for conformity with EEO program
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'appraise its personnel operations at regular intervals to assure their conformity with its program, this part 1614 and the instructions contained in the Commission's management directives.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate EEO Director, officers and special emphasis managers
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'designate a Director of Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO Director), EEO Officer(s), and such Special Emphasis Program Managers... clerical and administrative support as may be necessary' and the EEO Director shall be under immediate supervision of the agency head.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make written EEO materials available and post notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'make written materials available to all employees and applicants informing them of EEO programs and remedial procedures and prominently post such materials in personnel and EEO offices and throughout the workplace.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure cooperation with EEO Counselors and Commission investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'ensure that full cooperation is provided by all agency employees to EEO Counselors and agency EEO personnel... and that full cooperation is provided to the Commission ... including granting the Commission routine access to personnel records when required.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicize EEO Counselor and officer contact information and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must 'publicize to all employees and post at all times the names, business telephone numbers and business addresses of the EEO Counselors... a notice of the time limits and necessity of contacting a Counselor before filing a complaint and the telephone numbers and addresses of the EEO Director, EEO Officer(s) and Special Emphasis Program Managers.'

rubrics_metrics.name: EEO Director responsibilities: advise and develop plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The EEO Director shall advise the head of the agency on preparation of equal employment opportunity plans, procedures, regulations, reports and other matters pertaining to the policy in §1614.101 and the agency program.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEO Director responsibilities: evaluate sufficiency of program and recommend corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: The EEO Director shall 'evaluate from time to time the sufficiency of the total agency program for equal employment opportunity and report to the head of the agency with recommendations as to any improvement or correction needed, including remedial or disciplinary action with respect to managerial, supervisory or other employees who have failed in their responsibilities.'

rubrics_metrics.name: EEO Director responsibilities: implement changes to eliminate discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: When authorized by the head of the agency, the EEO Director may make changes in programs and procedures designed to eliminate discriminatory practices and to improve the agency's EEO program.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEO Director responsibilities: counseling and processing complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The EEO Director shall provide for counseling of aggrieved individuals and for the receipt and processing of individual and class complaints of discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEO Director responsibilities: ensure fair, timely investigations and final action
rubrics_metrics.description: The EEO Director shall 'assur[e] that individual complaints are fairly and thoroughly investigated and that final action is taken in a timely manner in accordance with this part.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered statutes for complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual and class complaints covered by this part include discrimination and retaliation prohibited by Title VII, the ADEA (age 40+), the Rehabilitation Act (disability), the Equal Pay Act (sex‑based wage discrimination), GINA (genetic information), and the PWFA (pregnancy‑related conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered agencies and units
rubrics_metrics.description: This part applies to military departments, executive agencies, United States Postal Service, Postal Rate Commission, Tennessee Valley Authority, certain judicial branch units (with exceptions), NOAA Commissioned Corps, Government Printing Office (except Rehabilitation Act), and the Smithsonian Institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered persons and employment actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Within covered departments and agencies this part applies to all employees and applicants for employment, and to all employment policies or practices affecting employees or applicants, including those paid from non‑appropriated funds, unless otherwise excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: This part does not apply to uniformed members of the military, employees of the GAO, employees of the Library of Congress, aliens employed outside the U.S., or certain Equal Pay Act complaints performed abroad or in certain territories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must adopt complaint processing procedures consistent with §§1614.105–1614.110
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall adopt procedures for processing individual and class complaints that include the provisions contained in §§1614.105 through 1614.110 and §1614.204 and that are consistent with all other applicable provisions of this part and the Commission's Management Directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission review of agency complaint processing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall periodically review agency resources and procedures to ensure reasonable efforts to resolve complaints informally, timely processing, adequate factual records, legally consistent decisions, explained reasons for decisions, and adequate notice to complainants of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory pre‑complaint counseling before filing a complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggrieved persons must consult a Counselor prior to filing a complaint in order to try to informally resolve the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: 45‑day contact requirement for counseling
rubrics_metrics.description: An aggrieved person must initiate contact with a Counselor within 45 days of the date of the matter alleged to be discriminatory or, for personnel actions, within 45 days of the effective date of the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency or Commission may extend the 45‑day limit for reasons including lack of notice, lack of knowledge, circumstances beyond control, or other sufficient reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counselor must advise rights and responsibilities in writing at initial session
rubrics_metrics.description: At the initial counseling session, Counselors must advise individuals in writing of their rights and responsibilities, including right to request a hearing or immediate final decision, election rights, duty to mitigate damages, time frames, and that only claims raised in pre‑complaint counseling (or like/related issues) may be alleged in a subsequent complaint. Counselors must also advise duty to keep addresses current and to serve copies of appeal papers on the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must include right to file class complaints and counselor must explain class complaint procedures if aggrieved person indicates desire to file a class complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to choose ADR instead of counseling and ADR timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Counselors shall advise aggrieved persons that, where the agency agrees to offer ADR in the case, they may choose between participation in ADR and the counseling activities; pre‑complaint processing period for ADR participants is 90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unresolved before the 90th day, the complainant will receive the notice of right to file a discrimination complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counselor must submit written report to agency and aggrieved person
rubrics_metrics.description: When advised that a complaint has been filed, the Counselor shall submit a written report within 15 days to the agency office designated to accept complaints and the aggrieved person concerning issues discussed and actions taken during counseling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counseling final interview and notice to file timeline (30/15 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the aggrieved person agrees to a longer counseling period or chooses ADR, the Counselor shall conduct the final interview within 30 days of contacting the EEO office. If not resolved, the Counselor shall inform the aggrieved person in writing by the 30th day of the right to file a discrimination complaint and that the complaint must be filed within 15 days of receipt of the notice; the acknowledgment will identify the official and advise of duty to inform agency if retaining counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional 60‑day counseling extension by written agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the end of the 30‑day period, the aggrieved person may agree in writing to postpone the final interview and extend counseling for an additional period of no more than 60 days; if unresolved at end of extension, the notice described in paragraph (d) must be issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counselor shall not restrain filing or reveal identity without authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: The Counselor shall not attempt to restrain the aggrieved person from filing a complaint and shall not reveal the identity of an aggrieved person who consulted the Counselor except when authorized or until the agency has received a discrimination complaint involving that same matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints must be filed with the agency alleged to have discriminated
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint must be filed with the agency that allegedly discriminated against the complainant.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15‑day filing period after receipt of counselor notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint must be filed within 15 days of receipt of the notice required by §1614.105(d), (e), or (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint must contain a signed statement from the person claiming to be aggrieved (or their attorney) sufficiently precise to identify the aggrieved individual and the agency and to describe generally the action(s) or practice(s) that form the basis of the complaint, plus a telephone number and address for contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint amendment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant may amend a complaint at any time prior to conclusion of the investigation to include issues or claims like or related to those raised in the complaint; after requesting a hearing the complainant may file a motion with the administrative judge to amend to include like/related issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency acknowledgment and notification of rights and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall acknowledge receipt of a complaint or amendment in writing, inform the complainant of the filing date, advise where a hearing request shall be sent, and advise that the complainant has the right to appeal final action or dismissal and that the agency must conduct an impartial investigation within 180 days unless parties agree to extend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a complaint is amended, investigation must be completed within the earlier of 180 days after last amendment or 360 days after original filing (subject to exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for dismissal of entire complaint prior to hearing (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to a request for a hearing, the agency shall dismiss an entire complaint if it meets specified dismissal grounds in §1614.107(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal ground: fails to state a claim or duplicative/pending claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Dismiss the complaint that 'fails to state a claim under §1614.103 or §1614.106(a) or states the same claim that is pending before or has been decided by the agency or Commission.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal ground: failure to comply with time limits or counseling requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Dismiss complaints that fail to comply with applicable time limits in §§1614.105, 1614.106 and 1614.204(c), unless extended by §1614.604(c), or that raise a matter not brought to the attention of a Counselor and not like/related to a counseled matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal ground: basis of pending civil action or decided civil action
rubrics_metrics.description: Dismiss complaints that are the basis of a pending civil action in U.S. District Court (provided 180 days have passed since filing administrative complaint) or that were the basis of a civil action decided by a district court in which the complainant was a party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal ground: election to pursue non‑EEO process (grievance/MSPB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dismiss complaints where the complainant raised the matter in a negotiated grievance procedure that permits discrimination allegations or in an appeal to the MSPB and the complainant has elected to pursue the non‑EEO process as indicated in §1614.301 or §1614.302.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal ground: mootness or proposed preliminary personnel action (unless retaliatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dismiss complaints that are moot or that allege a proposal to take a personnel action or other preliminary step unless the complaint alleges the proposal or preliminary step is retaliatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal ground: complainant cannot be located after reasonable efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Dismiss where the complainant cannot be located provided reasonable efforts were made and the complainant has not responded within 15 days to a notice of proposed dismissal sent to their last known address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal ground: failure to respond to agency requests for information/cooperate
rubrics_metrics.description: Dismiss where the agency provided a written request for relevant information or otherwise to proceed and the complainant failed to respond within 15 days or the response did not address the request (if the request included notice of proposed dismissal); instead of dismissal, case may be adjudicated if sufficient information exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal ground: dissatisfaction with processing of a prior complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Dismiss complaints that allege dissatisfaction with the processing of a previously filed complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal ground: misuse/abuse of EEO process (clear pattern of misuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dismiss where the agency, applying Commission criteria, finds the complaint is part of a clear pattern of misuse of the EEO process, which requires evidence of multiple filings and allegations that are similar or identical, lack specificity or involve previously resolved matters; evidence of circumventing other administrative processes, retaliating against in‑house processes, or overburdening the EEO system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial dismissal process and reviewability
rubrics_metrics.description: Where some but not all claims should be dismissed for reasons in §1614.107(a)(1)-(9), the agency shall notify the complainant in writing of determination and rationale and place copy in investigative file; this determination is reviewable by an administrative judge if a hearing is requested on the remainder, but not appealable until final action on the remainder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency conducts investigations of complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigation of complaints shall be conducted by the agency against which the complaint has been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigations must develop impartial and appropriate factual record
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall develop an impartial and appropriate factual record 'one that allows a reasonable fact finder to draw conclusions as to whether discrimination occurred.' Agencies may use letters, memoranda, interrogatories, fact‑finding conferences or other fact‑finding methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators are encouraged to incorporate ADR techniques into investigative efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production of documentary and testimonial evidence; oaths
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainant, agency, and any federal employee shall produce such documentary and testimonial evidence as the investigator deems necessary. Investigators are authorized to administer oaths. Statements must be under oath or by written statement under penalty of perjury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failure to respond to requests for information (adverse inferences and sanctions)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a party fails without good cause to respond fully and timely to requests for documents, records, comparative data, statistics, affidavits or witness attendance, the investigator may note that the decisionmaker or Commission may, in appropriate circumstances: (i) draw an adverse inference; (ii) consider matters established in favor of opposing party; (iii) exclude other evidence offered by the party failing to produce; (iv) issue a decision fully or partially in favor of the opposing party; or (v) take other appropriate actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators must have appropriate security clearances
rubrics_metrics.description: Any investigation will be conducted by investigators with appropriate security clearances; the Commission will supply names of investigators with appropriate clearances upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation completion within 180 days with limited extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall complete its investigation within 180 days of filing of an individual complaint (or within time in order from Office of Federal Operations). By written agreement the parties may extend up to 90 days. Agency may unilaterally extend up to 30 days to sanitize classified information, with notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant's right to investigative file and to request hearing within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 180 days from filing (or earlier of 180 after last amendment or 360 after original filing as applicable), the agency shall provide the complainant a copy of the investigative file and notify that within 30 days of receipt the complainant has the right to request a hearing and decision from an administrative judge or may request an immediate final decision from the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice shall inform that hearing request may be filed using the EEOC Public Portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency notice when unable to complete investigation in time and options for complainant
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency does not send the notice required within applicable time limits, it shall issue a written notice informing the complainant it has been unable to complete investigation and estimate completion date; the notice must explain that complainant may request a hearing or file a civil action in U.S. District Court instead of waiting, and must contain information about hearing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant may request hearing any time after 180 days or upon receiving notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the complainant has received the notice or at any time after 180 days have elapsed from filing, the complainant may request a hearing by submitting a written request to the EEOC office indicated, or through the EEOC Public Portal, and must send a copy to the agency EEO office; agency shall provide complaint file to EEOC within 15 days of receipt of hearing request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of administrative judge for hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complainant requests a hearing, the Commission shall appoint an administrative judge to conduct a hearing; upon appointment the AJ assumes full responsibility for adjudication including overseeing development of the record. Any hearing will be conducted by an AJ or hearing examiner with appropriate security clearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative judge may dismiss complaints pursuant to §1614.107
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative judges may dismiss complaints pursuant to §1614.107 on their own initiative, after notice to the parties, or upon an agency's motion to dismiss a complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer of resolution rules and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may make an offer of resolution any time after filing but not later than date an AJ is appointed (for attorney‑represented complainants), and any time after appointment but not later than 30 days prior to hearing. Offers must be in writing and include notice explaining consequences of failing to accept. To be effective an agency's offer must include attorney's fees and costs and specify non‑monetary relief; monetary relief may be lump sum or itemized. Complainant has 30 days to accept; failure to accept and later receiving less favorable relief may forfeit payment of attorney's fees or costs incurred after the 30‑day period except where interest of justice requires otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance must be in writing and timely if postmarked/received within 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery rights and AJ authority to limit discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The AJ shall notify parties of right to seek discovery and may issue discovery orders as appropriate. Unless parties agree, the party seeking discovery must request authorization from the AJ prior to commencing discovery. Both parties are entitled to reasonable development of evidence relevant to issues but AJ may limit quantity and timing of discovery. Evidence may be developed through interrogatories, depositions, requests for admissions, stipulations or production of documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: 'investigation', 'hearing', 'final action', 'basis of alleged discrimination', 'issue of alleged discrimination'
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 1614 defines key procedural terms: 'investigation' (as in §§1614.108/1614.106(e)(2)), 'hearing' (as in §1614.109), 'final action by an agency' (as in §1614.110), and 'basis of alleged discrimination' which lists protected categories (race, color, religion, reprisal, sex, national origin, Equal Pay Act, age, disability, genetic information, pregnancy/related conditions). 'Issue of alleged discrimination' is defined by the EEOC Standard Form 462 categories (appointment/hire; assignment of duties; awards; conversion to full time; disciplinary actions including demotion, reprimand, suspension, removal; duty hours; evaluation/appraisal; examination/test; harassment non‑sexual/sexual; medical examination; pay/overtime; promotion/non‑selection; reassignment denied/directed; reasonable accommodation; reinstatement; retirement; termination; terms/conditions; time and attendance; training; other).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data posting formats and accessibility (No FEAR Act data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall post statistical data in PDF and an accessible text format that complies with section 508; prominently post the date last updated; include separate data for each subordinate component; title data 'Equal Employment Opportunity Data Posted Pursuant to Title III of the Notification and Federal Employee Antidiscrimination and Retaliation Act of 2002 (No FEAR Act)' and post a hyperlink 'No FEAR Act Data' on an agency homepage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies shall ensure data can be readily accessed through commercial search engines. Processing times must be recorded using number of days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not post separate quarterly statistics for current fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall post cumulative data for the current fiscal year and may not post separate quarterly statistics for the current fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use EEOC template for agencies with 100+ employees and subordinate components
rubrics_metrics.description: Data posted by agencies having 100 or more employees, and all subordinate component data, shall be presented in the manner and order set forth in the template EEOC has placed for this purpose on its public web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template rules include vertical columns for fiscal years (oldest leftmost), horizontal rows for categories as listed in §1614.704(a)-(m), ordering of bases and issues as in §1614.702, 'non‑EEO basis' last after 'disability', and specific arrangements when posting certain categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide URL for posted data to Commission within 60 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days of the effective date of this rule, an agency shall provide the Commission the URL for the data it posts under this subpart; thereafter new or changed URLs must be provided within 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record processing times in number of days
rubrics_metrics.description: Processing times required to be posted shall be recorded using number of days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to be posted — number of complaints filed (metric a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Federal agency shall post the number of complaints filed in such fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting is current fiscal year, quarterly schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to be posted — number of individuals filing complaints (metric b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post the number of individuals filing those complaints (including as the agent of a class).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to be posted — number filing two or more complaints (metric c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post the number of individuals who filed two or more of those complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to be posted — counts by bases of alleged discrimination (metric d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post the number of complaints, whether initially or through amendment, raising each of the various bases of alleged discrimination and the number in which a non‑EEO basis is alleged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bases must be arranged in order they appear in §1614.702(j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to be posted — counts by issues of alleged discrimination (metric e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post the number of complaints, whether initially or through amendment, raising each of the various issues of alleged discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues must be arranged as in §1614.702(k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to be posted — average processing times (metric f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish the average length of time it has taken the agency to complete, respectively, investigation and final action by an agency for: (1) all complaints pending for any length of time during the fiscal year; (2) all complaints pending during the fiscal year in which a hearing was not requested; and (3) all complaints during the fiscal year in which a hearing was requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to be posted — number and time to dismissal (metric g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post the number of complaints dismissed by an agency pursuant to §1614.107(a), and the average length of time such complaints had been pending prior to dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to be posted — number withdrawn by complainants (metric h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post the number of complaints withdrawn by complainants during the fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to be posted — final actions involving finding of discrimination (metric i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post the total number of final actions by an agency rendered in such fiscal year involving a finding of discrimination and, of that number, the number and percentage that were rendered without a hearing and the number and percentage that were rendered after a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to be posted — distribution of findings by basis (metric j)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the total number of final actions involving a finding of discrimination, post (1) the number and percentage based on each respective basis; (2) the number and percentage for each basis rendered without a hearing; and (3) the number and percentage for each basis rendered after a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to be posted — distribution of findings by issue (metric k)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the total number of final actions involving a finding of discrimination, post (1) the number and percentage for each respective issue; (2) the number and percentage for each issue rendered without a hearing; and (3) the number and percentage for each issue rendered after a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to be posted — pendency breakdown by process stage (metric l)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the total number of complaints pending for any length of time in such fiscal year, post (1) the number that were first filed before the start of the then current fiscal year, and of those (i) the number of individuals who filed those complaints, and (ii) the number that are pending at investigation, hearing, final action by an agency, and appeal steps of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to be posted — complaints with overdue investigations (metric m)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the total number of complaints pending for any length of time in such fiscal year, post the total number of complaints in which the agency has not completed its investigation within the time required by 29 CFR 1614.106(e)(2) plus any authorized extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative year‑end data requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Commencing Jan 31, 2004 and annually by Jan 31 thereafter, each Federal agency shall post year‑end data corresponding to §1614.704 for each of the five immediately preceding fiscal years (or however many of five for which data are available). For each category post a separate figure per fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other data must not be included with No FEAR Act data
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall not include or otherwise post with the data required under §§1614.704 and 1614.705 any other data, whether or not EEO related, though such other data may be posted on a separate page.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEOC posting requirements for hearings statistics (EEOC data — hearings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall post quarterly current fiscal year statistics regarding hearings: number of hearings requested, number of individuals filing those requests, individuals filing two or more requests, number of hearing requests involving each basis and each issue, average time to complete hearing step for all cases pending at hearing step, number of AJ decisions rendered involving finding of discrimination and portion without/after hearing, distributions by basis and issue, numbers first filed before current fiscal year and associated individuals, and total number where Commission failed to complete hearing step within §1614.109(i) time.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEOC posting requirements for appeals statistics (EEOC data — appeals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall post quarterly current fiscal year statistics regarding appeals: number of appeals filed, number of individuals filing those appeals, number filing two or more appeals, number of appeals raising each basis and each issue, average time EEOC to issue appellate decisions (for all appeals and split by whether hearing requested), numbers of appellate decisions involving findings of discrimination with breakdowns by agency final action timing (without/after hearing) and by basis and issue, and pendency figures for appeals filed before current fiscal year.
